children: A selloff in CoreWeave's corporate bonds — magnified by a social media post — triggered a sharp drop in the artificial-intelligence stock on Wednesday. The bond rout signals credit investor worries about the AI infrastructure provider's mounting debt burden and future borrowing costs.

Shares fell 15% to $65.78, their lowest close since hitting $60.82 on July 29, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The stock is off 8% for the year, tracking its worst year on record, and is down 24% in October.

Coreweave's 9.625% notes, due in 2032, were trading at $79.50, down from $85 at the start of the month, according to the TRACE bond pricing information service. The bond's yield has climbed to 15.06% from 13.42% those two weeks.

Weakness extended across CoreWeave's other bonds. Its 9.75% notes, due in 2031, were trading at $81.48, down from about $87 on Oct. 1; its 9.25% notes, due in 2030, fell to $88.25 from roughly $94. Their yields climbed to 15.2% and 13.44%, respectively, from 13.44% and 11.55%.
The social media post came from venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya late Tuesday. He wrote: Coreweave's bond yield touched 15% today, then closed at a new high.
That prompted a single-word response from Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk: "Yikes."
A couple of hours earlier, Palihapitiya cross-posted a long warning from his Social Capital website about the reliance of debt to finance the AI infrastructure buildout.
CoreWeave operates data centers and rents computing capacity to companies developing and running AI models.
One of CoreWeave's biggest partners is Nvidia, which is both a chip supplier and an investor. Nvidia's stake in CoreWeave is about $3.1 billion.
Nvidia's backing has helped fuel CoreWeave's rapid expansion, but building the infrastructure to meet growing AI demand has required billions of dollars in borrowing.
CoreWeave issued $2 billion in senior notes carrying a 9.25% interest rate in May 2025, then $1.75 billion in notes paying 9% two months later.
This year, the company issued $2.75 billion in notes paying 9.75% in April and $1.25 billion paying 9.625% in June.
In August 2023, the company secured a $2.3 billion loan backed by Nvidia chips and other assets, carrying an effective interest rate of roughly 15%. It matures in March 2028.
